product_brief: Free, open-source software adding post-quantum secure key exchange to WireGuard VPN using Classic McEliece and Kyber.
pqc_capability_description: Rosenpass implements a post-quantum-secure authenticated key exchange using Classic McEliece and Kyber. It generates keys supplied to WireGuard as pre-shared symmetric keys (PSK) for hybrid post-quantum security. It is a reference implementation written in Rust, using libsodium and liboqs. It provides security against state disruption attacks via a stateless responder.
key_management_model: Post-quantum-secure authenticated key exchange; generates shared secrets supplied as pre-shared symmetric keys (PSK) to WireGuard; stateless responder using encrypted cookies.
architecture_type: Add-on software running alongside WireGuard; stand-alone tool for key exchange; reference implementation.
pqc_roadmap_details: Uses Classic McEliece and Kyber; cryptographic proof of security is in the works; symbolic analysis provided using ProVerif.
implementation_attack_surface: Uses variable colouring (gating use of a secret value through a `.secret()` method); code zeroises all key material; written in Rust.
testing_&_validation_methods: Symbolic analysis of the protocol using ProVerif; reference implementation in Rust.
supply_chain_&_vendor_risk: Uses C libraries libsodium and liboqs; open-source with public GitHub repository; Apache 2.0 and MIT licensed.
deployment_&_migration_complexity: Easy to install and maintain alongside WireGuard; runs on the side supplying keys; executes new handshake every two minutes.
